item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 5 August 2026
item.description:
Ocho spins a lively Tales of Argosa recap as Orluf Wavebane’s new party battles Urgot and explores a temple tied to a previous campaign.

Tipa’s Frosthaven crew finally drops the Chaos Lord atop the spire, juggling nasty light, spark swarms, traps, and looming retirement plans.

Nimgimli likes Hell is Us’s moody world, puzzles, and story hook, but bails when no map, markers, or journal turn immersion into homework.

Littlelum digs into forum gaming, spotlighting Mafia and how slower phases, PMs, and text play make social deduction weirder and deeper online.

Ramen Junkie checks out a bizarre five-bot gun combiner with clunky kibble, Gobots vibes, and just enough absurdity to justify the impulse buy.

Luna’s July log mixes creative highs with lighter gaming, including Rhythm Paradise Groove, Ghost Trick, Fortune Fragments, and Minishoot’ Adventures.

Oya finds Final Fantasy VI still hits hard, praising its ensemble cast, solid story, and Kefka despite some very 1994-style storytelling shortcuts.

David’s Dragonbane party hacks through skeletons and hidden crossbowmen in the dwarven realm, then finds clear signs the Ravens were there first.

Wilhelm riffs on RuneScape Monopoly and why no special edition skin can make Monopoly feel less like, well, Monopoly.

Tim Bray pairs reflective garden photos with a blunt bit of political despair, then lands on calm water as a small way to steady yourself.

WCRobinson makes a heartfelt case for human writing in the Blaugust era, pushing back on social-media churn and generative AI creep.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 4 August 2026
item.description:
Syp recaps a comfy month of LOTRO and Guild Wars 2, then eyes more completionist hobbiting while debating a GW2 break for FFXIV or Stars Reach.

Scopique weighs Star Citizen instancing as a tradeoff between curated story control and the sandbox spirit, with hangar jank still looming.

Wilhelm side-eyes LOTRO’s oddly unannounced Wolves of Mordor expansion and its new Mordor-only Survival Instincts talent tree, sounding more puzzled than impressed.

The Friendly Necromancer gets won over by EverQuest Legends, especially its wild three-class multiclassing that turns Beastlord dreams into reality.

Wolfy comes away mostly happy from FFXIV Berlin Fan Fest, especially about Evercold’s Bastion tank, airship zones, and the FFVII raids.

Tipa tours Manchester’s Cruisin’ Main Street, mixing working-class car show vibes with fond, funny memories of Beetles, Miatas, and a fuel-hungry Supra.

Warner finds Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey good but not great, praising the spectacle while feeling the intimate scenes and lead casting miss.

Wakupan shares beloved treasures, from Taiwanese risograph art and glassware to a favorite mug, cat painting, and irresistibly cute glass flower.

Sid argues DeepSeek V4 Flash and recent LLM price cuts are making AI coding help absurdly cheap, practical, and hard to ignore.

Roger uses a Blaugust prompt to revisit his first blog, early film reviews, and the old lesson to write what you know.

Frostilyte salutes Blaugust, reflects on encouraging feedback, and gushes over Titanium Court’s clever match-3-meets-strategy design.

Bhagpuss uses Blaugust to mull blogging for yourself, reader expectations, and the tempting fantasy of turning the blog into a private club.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 3 August 2026
item.description:
Tipa wonders why EverQuest Legends promises new lore when EverQuest still does such a shaky job explaining places like Crushbone, Befallen, Runnyeye, and Najena.

Magi is hooked on Celestial Decks, praising its deep deckbuilding, mind games, and actual human-made art in a crowded CCG field.

Shintar reflects on WoW Classic nostalgia, from Barrens shower flashbacks to missing that old Burning Crusade feeling without wanting today’s Classic modes.

Wes says MiSTer’s new Console Mode finally makes the FPGA box feel like a proper console, with fast performance and flexible views.

Ellie finds Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter polished but awfully familiar, more like a refined expansion than a big leap forward.

Wilhelm says Halo: Campaign Evolved shipped at 83.3, boosting his Fantasy Critic lead while counter-picking Bhagpuss took the hit.

Tan loved the Miyoo Flip for retro gaming and TV play, but repeated hinge failures turned that clamshell dream into a pricey heartbreak.

UltrViolet shares an uncomfortable neck MRI, some blog-comment tinkering, and the weary hope that the scan might finally explain the arm issues.

Kluwes celebrates a new local comic shop, happily digging through back issues and leaving with Locke & Key and family goodwill.

Aneesh maps out Thickets, Places, Spaces, and Portals as a way to get intellectually lost without just wandering aimlessly.

Margot ditched her self-hosted site to get back to writing, then shares why Splatoon Raiders clicked as a stylish, bite-sized Switch 2 favorite.

Jeromai uses an AI-written letter on “enough” to argue for a calmer, less all-consuming Blaugust pace this year.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 2 August 2026
item.description:
Tipa says real-time Captain Sonar is gloriously chaotic, with the Radio Operator doing the real detective work while sudden death keeps every mistake lethal.

Dávid enjoyed Bombanana!’s three-player bomb-defusal chaos on Linux, praising its clever communication twist while noting rough edges like uncapped FPS.

Joar is taking another Blaugust swing with daily posts on WoW expansions, MMOs, blogging, and altoholic habits, partly to honor Belghast.

owls dives into Everquest Legends on Freeport, enjoying the grind and goofy tutorial NPCs despite crowding, deaths, and instance hiccups.

Azuriel muses on how random discovery shapes favorite music, games, and books, and why algorithms rarely replace genuine serendipity.

Joel rounds up a busy July of games, movies, podcasts, and soccer, with Transistor, Monument Valley, and The Odyssey among the highlights.

Ghastly starts Blaugust with plans for community-minded posting while juggling a move, house projects, and dreams of a garden and maybe chickens.

Welsh Troll bumps his blog’s font size, rethemes the site, and cleans up CSS and semantic HTML in a readability-first overhaul.

Cristian built AntiSearch in Calamus: a small, category-based link directory meant to dodge SEO sludge with simple local filtering and optional info tabs.

Aywren joins Blaugust in Belghast’s memory, focusing on community support and boosting posts through the event’s Mastodon account.

Wilhelm kicks off Blaugust by reflecting on how the event shaped his longer, less link-dumpy blogging habits over the years.

Blockade85 opens Blaugust with a personal intro and a promise of a month of opinions, games, sports, books, music, and whatever else shows up.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 1 August 2026
item.description:
Krista gives a handy primer on Fields of Mistria 1.0, covering its farming, magic, romance, festivals, and cozy life-sim hooks.

Wilhelm checks in on Warp Point’s old-school gaming webring idea, plus the familiar headaches around discoverability, WordPress limits, and AI rules.

Jimmy announces a 1999 ebook and previews a stacked year ahead with The Sims, Deus Ex, Diablo II, Anno 1602, and more.

Andrew Plotkin releases Visible Suspended, bringing Infocom’s robot-juggling cryogenic nightmare to the browser with recreated map art and source code.

Anarchae’s weekly digest mixes job-search annoyance with thoughts on sci-fi anthologies, Ayatsuji mysteries, Taskmaster, Traitors, and more Zelda.

Tobold muses on holidays after retirement, arguing crowded Instagram tourism is miserable and quieter, off-season trips make more sense.

Tofutush dives into Umineko EP1–4 with a delightfully frantic pile of red-text theories, locked-room questions, and Beatrice-related brain melt.

Jamie Zawinski unloads on San Francisco’s expanding police surveillance push, from drones to businesses being nudged into camera-sharing partnerships.

Jeff pushes his Mac Studio to 25 GbE over Thunderbolt, then wrestles with iperf3 limits and a NIC enclosure running dangerously hot.

Bruce spotlights the Squid microscope, which helped researchers discover 31 new marine species in just two weeks.

Brennan offers a timely Blaugust reminder: your site doesn’t need a blog, and creative life doesn’t have to be gamified into posting quotas.

CrazyKinux reflects on Silo Season 3 as a book reader, mourning how adaptation changes make the show feel like a different story.
